column1: # Where each source database is obtained. Single source of truth: food_DBs/SOURCE.md files
# are GENERATED from this table by food_DBs/write_source_stubs.py — edit here, not there.
# The raw releases are not redistributed with this repository. Their terms differ by source
# (some NonCommercial, some ShareAlike, NEVO by written permission covering derived values
# only), so each is fetched from its provider. The rights themselves live in
# 5_export/licence_tiers.csv, which is also Supplementary Table S1 of the Data Descriptor —
# do not restate a licence here or the two will drift.
# version_used is the release THIS build ingested. A newer release usually still ingests, but
# component columns move between versions and the ingest maps them by name, so check the
# ingest's unmapped-column report after any upgrade.

column8: The relational CSV set. A 2026 release exists on open.canada.ca; this build ingested 2015.
Exported from the open-data interface rather than shipped as a fixed file, so the filename is ours.
The export carries the source's editing layer alongside the reference set; the ingest drops the copy records (see food_DBs/_common/non_nutrients.py).
Four language editions are offered; this build used English.

column3: STFCJ (Standard Tables of Food Composition in Japan)
column8: Follow the 日本食品標準成分表2020年版（八訂） link, then its Excel downloads. The English mirror that served these file ids has been retired.
Download dataset on the site; the .ods twin in this folder is the same release.
Composition data only; the metabolism and processing tables are not ingested.
Nutrient profiles workbook, not the per-food search export.

column3: WAFCT (Food Composition Table for Western Africa)
column8: Listed on the FAO/INFOODS databases page as "FAO/INFOODS Food Composition Table for Western Africa (2019)".
Same FAO/INFOODS page as PhyFoodComp and WAFCT.

column3: PhyFoodComp (Global Food Composition Database for Phytate)
column8: Same FAO/INFOODS page as BioFoodComp and WAFCT.

Request the dataset from RIVM; it is free. The release itself is in neither this repository nor the deposit — RIVM asked that users be sent to their download page. 5_export/reconstruct_nevo.py rebuilds the NEVO partition from it.
Authored here, not fetched: HMOs, sialic acid, fucose, xylan, arabinoxylan, dextran, pullulan, cellobiose, alginate, agarose and related substrates that composition tables omit.
